summary.text: Michael C. Walsh, a Republican general-practice attorney and Lynnfield native with about 15 years of practice, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Massachusetts to Andrea Campbell.
At the time he was litigating cases against the Attorney General's office.

paragraphs.text: Walsh was born and raised in Lynnfield. He earned his bachelor's degree at 17 and his law degree at 21 at Suffolk University, which his campaign calls the youngest graduate in school history.
He is a general-practice litigator whose work includes public employment and labor law, criminal defense, military law, administrative procedure, land use and zoning.

Walsh was the Republican nominee for the 5th District seat on the Governor's Council in 2022 and lost the general election to Eileen R. Duff. In 2026 he won the Republican primary for attorney general with no opponent, according to the state Elections Division.
During the campaign, he emphasized enforcing a legislative audit law, local control of zoning and lower utility bills.
He received 34.4% of the vote to Andrea Campbell's 65.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
